summary: The Insurance Commissioner runs the Department of Insurance: approving or rejecting rate increases under Proposition 103, licensing insurers and agents, and overseeing the FAIR Plan, the insurer of last resort that has grown as companies pull back from wildfire-prone areas. The seat is open: Ricardo Lara is term-limited. Both finalists are Democrats. Former San Francisco supervisor Jane Kim placed first in the June 2 primary with 27.40%; state Senator Ben Allen placed second with 19.41%.

positions.stance: Proposes 'natural disaster insurance for all', a premium-funded state authority guaranteeing wildfire and flood coverage, while keeping a more accountable FAIR Plan as insurer of last resort. (CalMatters voter guide)
Would tie insurers' ability to sell auto insurance in California to their willingness to write home insurance. (CalMatters)
Would freeze rates when a policyholder files a claim, penalize claim delays, and publish a dashboard of insurers' claims records. (CalMatters)
Would expand the state's low-cost auto insurance program to more drivers. (CalMatters)
Pledged not to accept insurance-industry contributions. (Wikipedia)
After the Los Angeles County fires hit his district, authored bills to give the department more enforcement power and to create a wildfire-resilience loan program. (CalMatters voter guide)

Would require insurers to report claim delays and outstanding claims in real time after disasters and explain denials; would add complaint staff and a consumer advocate inside the department. (CalMatters)
Wants more oversight of the FAIR Plan and more accountability to the department. (CalMatters)
Favors home and community mitigation, avoiding new building in high-fire-risk areas, and encouraging people to move out of them. (CalMatters)
Opposes opening the low-cost auto program to everyone, arguing it could hurt the low-income drivers it serves. (CalMatters)

key_differences: Structure: Kim would create a new state-run disaster insurance authority; Allen would work within the existing market with tougher oversight and mitigation incentives.
Leverage over insurers: Kim would condition auto-insurance licenses on writing home policies; Allen has not proposed that.
Low-cost auto insurance: Kim would expand eligibility; Allen opposes opening it to everyone.
Background: Kim is a former supervisor, organizer, and consumer advocate; Allen is a sitting legislator with a long environmental record, including authoring the 2024 Proposition 4 climate bond.
